messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT — Elevated 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (5m error rate 8%, spike at 12:34 UTC). Threshold exceeded. Paging maria (oncall). Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/prod/alerts/1932104567

maria (oncall): I'm oncall, joining. I'm seeing errors are mostly 502/504 gateway timeouts. Starting live tail and checking routing.

jay (eng-runtime): FYI we deployed a route weight + retry policy tweak ~25m ago to reduce p95 by favouring cached pool. Could be related.

maria (oncall): running quick curl against gateway to reproduce: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'` — getting 502 with empty body.

liam (sre): checking envoy stats: `curl -sS http://localhost:9901/stats | grep upstream_cx_*` — seeing upstream connection failures and LB requeues for cluster model-serving-primary.

alex (infra): looking at control plane: the route to cluster `model-serving-primary` has `max_retries: 3` and `per_try_timeout_ms: 1000` — that can trigger retry storms if upstream is slow. Also circuit_breakers for that cluster have `max_connections: 100` and `max_pending_requests: 50` — they look small for current qps.

maria (oncall): hypothesis: retries + tight circuit breakers => retry amplification causing overloaded backends -> 5xx. What can we do quickly?

jay (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: 1) disable retries at the gateway for /v1/generate, 2) redirect some weight away from primary pool to fallback (cached) pool, 3) increase circuit breaker pending request limit. I'll start with disable retries and weight shift.

liam (sre): agree. Do the disable first (least risky). Patch via control-plane API:
```
PATCH /api/controlplane/routes/model-serving
{
  "route": {
    "retry_policy": { "num_retries": 0 }
  }
}
```
(we apply via infra-runbook script `infra/ctl route patch --name model-serving --retries 0`)

alex (infra): running the patch now — applying to edge gateways in region us-west-2. Rolling restart not required; changes pushed to xds.

sophie (support): heads up to support: preparing customer comms. Which customers are impacted?

maria (oncall): checking error-rate by customer: from logs higher than 5% error windows: cust-42, cust-87, cust-omega, and a few smaller ones. Sophie, could you open an incident note and start outreach to any active paid customers with >5% impact?

sophie (support): on it. Drafting short status: "We are investigating elevated 5xx on inference endpoint; mitigation in progress; more updates in 15m." Will post on status page.

jay (eng-runtime): after disabling retries I'm going to shift route weights: set primary -> 30% and cached-fallback -> 70% for 10m to relieve primary and see behavior. Command (control plane):
```
infra/ctl route update-weight --route model-serving --weights primary:30,fallback:70 --ttl 600
```

maria (oncall): executed both changes, turning down retries and shifting weights now. Watching graphs.

liam (sre): also bumping circuit breaker pending limit for model-serving-primary from 50 -> 200 quickly via patch so in-flight requests won't hit CB hard.

alex (infra): applied CB bump. Note: it's a short-term band-aid; need proper sizing + autoscale.

maria (oncall): error rate dropping — current 5m error rate 1.2% down from 8%. p95 latency also improving.

sophie (support): posted status: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/1932104567 — message sent to affected customers list.

jay (eng-runtime): we should also check for a config drift — why did retry policy change? Was it a manual edit or a rollout of a config bundle?

maria (oncall): quick check of recent commits: `git log --pretty=oneline infra/routes | head` shows a commit 26m ago by `sam-deployer` that updated `retry_policy` in `routes/model-serving.yaml`.

liam (sre): adding to timeline: 12:10 UTC deploy modifies retry policy -> 12:34 spike starts -> 12:35 alert triggers -> 12:38 retries disabled + weight shift -> 12:45 CB bump -> 12:49 errors down.

maria (oncall): handoff note for next oncall: mitigation applied, monitoring in steady state but we need a full postmortem and a revert or safer config approach (gradual canary + canary-rules). Leaving follow-up tasks: revert route to previous safe values, add pre-deploy load test for retry changes, add automated rollback when error rate >2% in 5m.

jay (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR that reverts the risky retry default and adds an explicit canary rollout flag; will include unit test for retry amplification scenario.

sophie (support): summary for customers: "We briefly experienced elevated 5xx on the inference endpoint caused by a routing/retry config change. We've mitigated by disabling retries and shifting traffic; affected customers have been contacted. We'll follow up with a root cause and timeline."

alex (infra): final check: no degraded nodes in primary pool, CPU & mem okay. We'll keep the weight shift for 20 minutes, then gradually move back if stable.

maria (oncall): last metrics: 5m error rate 0.6%, client-visible error volume dropped by ~85%. Closing the immediate pager. Marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. Postmortem required.

liam (sre): :white_check_mark: Good mitigation. Action items: (1) PR revert retry default (jay), (2) postmortem draft (maria+liam), (3) improve CB autosizing (alex), (4) support follow-ups (sophie). I'll assign and track.

sophie (support): I'll follow up with customer replies in thread and update the status page after the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident recorded: 1932104567 — severity: high — status: mitigated. Oncall: maria (maria@redwood.com).

maria (oncall): handing off to next oncall in 20m; leaving context + actions in the incident doc. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
